faqs.question: Is my money safe with CircleUp?
faqs.answer: Yes. CircleUp never holds your money—funds flow directly between members via Stripe, a PCI-DSS Level 1 certified payment processor. Your payment information is tokenized and encrypted. We're also regulated under Swiss FINMA requirements and fully GDPR compliant.

faqs.question: What happens if someone doesn't pay?
faqs.answer: Our Emergency Fund protects your circle. Every contribution includes a small amount (typically 1%) that goes into a pooled protection fund. If a member misses a payment, the Emergency Fund covers it so payouts continue on schedule. The defaulting member then repays the fund over time.

faqs.question: Are there any hidden fees?
faqs.answer: No hidden fees, ever. We charge a transparent platform fee (2-3% depending on your plan) on each contribution. This covers payment processing, the Emergency Fund, and all platform features. You see the exact fee before every payment.

faqs.question: How do you verify members?
faqs.answer: We offer multiple verification levels: email verification (basic), phone verification, and full KYC with government ID. Our AI Trust Score also analyzes payment history, tenure, and other factors to rate member reliability from 0-1000.

faqs.question: How do I join a circle?
faqs.answer: You can join a circle in three ways: accept an invitation from an organizer, browse public circles and request to join, or get invited via a referral link. Once accepted, set up your payment method and you're ready to start contributing.

faqs.question: When will I receive my payout?
faqs.answer: Your payout date is determined when you join the circle, based on the payout method (fixed order, random draw, bidding, or Trust Score). You can see your scheduled payout date in the app at any time. Payouts are typically disbursed within 1-2 business days.

faqs.question: Can I leave a circle early?
faqs.answer: You can request to leave a circle, but it depends on where you are in the cycle. If you've already received your payout, you're committed to completing your contributions. If you haven't received your payout yet, the organizer can approve your exit and find a replacement member.

faqs.question: What payment methods can I use?
faqs.answer: We accept credit/debit cards, bank transfers (SEPA), and TWINT in Switzerland. You can set up automatic payments so you never miss a contribution, or pay manually each time—your choice.

faqs.question: Am I liable if someone defaults?
faqs.answer: No. As an organizer, you're not personally liable for member defaults. The Emergency Fund handles defaults automatically. Your role is to manage the circle, not guarantee payments. CircleUp's structure protects both organizers and members.

faqs.question: How do I vet new members?
faqs.answer: Use our AI Trust Score to evaluate potential members. You can see their payment history, verification level, tenure on the platform, and overall reliability score (0-1000). You can also require minimum Trust Scores to join your circle.

faqs.question: Can I customize the circle rules?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. You control contribution amounts, frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly), payout order method, maximum members, Emergency Fund rate, late payment penalties, and more. Configure your circle to match your community's traditions.

faqs.question: What if I need to remove a member?
faqs.answer: You can remove members who consistently default or violate circle rules. The system handles the financial reconciliation—any amounts owed are tracked and the member's payout position is reassigned. You maintain full control of your circle's membership.

howItWorks.description: Everyone contributes the same amount each period. Payments are collected automatically and tracked transparently. No chasing, no spreadsheets.

howItWorks.title: Receive Your Payout
howItWorks.description: Each period, one member receives the full pot. Payouts continue until everyone has received their lump sum. Protected by our Emergency Fund.

member.question: Your circle contribution is due tomorrow but you just realized you don't have enough in your account. What should you do?

options.text: Wait and hope no one notices you're late
Contact the organizer immediately to discuss options
Leave the circle to avoid embarrassment
Ask another member to cover for you secretly

feedback.correct: Great choice! Proactive communication helps organizers plan. CircleUp's Emergency Fund can also cover temporary shortfalls.
feedback.incorrect: Communication is key in savings circles. CircleUp makes it easy to notify organizers and the Emergency Fund provides backup protection.

member.question: You're invited to join a circle with people you don't know personally. How do you evaluate if it's trustworthy?

options.text: Join anyway—what's the worst that could happen?
Decline—only join circles with people you know
Check the organizer's Trust Score and circle completion history
Ask for members' personal financial details

feedback.correct: CircleUp's Trust Score (0-1000) helps you evaluate members you haven't met. Check completion rates and payment history before joining.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp's Trust Score analyzes payment history, verification status, and more to help you evaluate members objectively.

member.question: What's the main advantage of automated payments in a savings circle?

options.text: You can skip payments when you want to
You never forget or miss a contribution
The organizer can't see your payment status
You pay less in fees

feedback.correct: Exactly! Automatic payments mean peace of mind. Set it up once and your contributions happen on schedule every time.
feedback.incorrect: Automated payments ensure you never miss a contribution—the number one cause of circle problems.

member.question: A member in your circle just received their payout but mentions they might stop contributing. What happens?

options.text: Nothing—they already got their money
They're committed to complete contributions; Emergency Fund covers if needed
The circle immediately ends for everyone
Other members have to cover their share

feedback.correct: Once you receive a payout, you're committed to completing your contributions. If they can't pay, the Emergency Fund covers other members.
feedback.incorrect: Members who've received payouts must complete their contributions. CircleUp's Emergency Fund protects the circle if they default.

member.question: How can you improve your Trust Score on CircleUp?

options.text: Pay your connections to vouch for you
Make on-time payments, verify your identity, and stay engaged
Join as many circles as possible at once
Trust Scores can't be improved

feedback.correct: Your Trust Score improves with consistent on-time payments (40%), identity verification (20%), platform tenure (15%), and engagement (10%).
feedback.incorrect: Trust Score is earned through behavior: on-time payments, verification, tenure, and positive engagement all contribute.

member.question: You want to join a circle but the minimum Trust Score requirement is higher than yours. What can you do?

options.text: Create a fake profile with a higher score
Start with a beginner circle to build your score first
There's nothing you can do
Complain to the organizer until they let you in

feedback.correct: Great thinking! Starter circles have lower Trust Score requirements and help you build history for higher-tier circles.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp offers starter circles with lower Trust Score requirements. Complete a few successfully to build your reputation.

member.question: What information can you see about your circle's finances?

options.text: Only your own contributions
Nothing—the organizer handles everything privately
All contributions, payouts, and the Emergency Fund balance
Other members' bank account details

feedback.correct: Full transparency! You can see every contribution, every payout, and the Emergency Fund balance. No secrets, no surprises.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp provides complete transparency—every member can see all contributions, payouts, and fund balances in real-time.

member.question: The organizer announces they need to change the contribution due date. How is this handled?

options.text: The organizer changes it unilaterally
All members vote on the change
The circle must be cancelled and restarted
Only new members are affected

feedback.correct: Major changes require member agreement. CircleUp's voting feature lets everyone have a say in circle modifications.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp's governance features ensure all members can vote on significant changes to circle terms.

member.question: Why might you choose a circle with 'Trust Score' payout order instead of fixed order?

options.text: It's completely random
Members with higher Trust Scores get priority, rewarding reliable behavior
The organizer always gets paid first
There's no difference

feedback.correct: Trust Score payout order rewards reliable members with earlier payouts, incentivizing good behavior throughout the circle.
feedback.incorrect: Trust Score payout order gives priority to members with proven reliability, creating incentives for on-time payments.

member.question: You receive your payout. What should you do with the funds?

options.text: Spend it all immediately—you earned it!
Use it for your savings goal, and continue contributing until the circle completes
Lend it to other circle members
Withdraw from the circle since you got your money

feedback.correct: Perfect! Use the payout for your goal, and remember—you're committed to contributing until everyone has received their payout.
feedback.incorrect: Your payout is for your savings goal, but remember your commitment continues until all members have received their payouts.

organizer.question: A member with a low Trust Score wants to join your circle. What's the best approach?

options.text: Reject them immediately—low scores mean trouble
Accept them but require additional verification or a smaller contribution
Accept everyone to fill the circle faster
Ask them to pay double contributions

feedback.correct: Smart approach! You can accept members conditionally—require enhanced KYC or start them in a smaller circle to build trust.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp lets you set custom requirements. Consider requiring additional verification for lower-Trust Score applicants.

organizer.question: Two members in your circle have a personal dispute. How should you handle it?

options.text: Ignore it—personal matters aren't your concern
Kick both members out immediately
Mediate professionally and document any issues affecting the circle
Take sides with the member you know better

feedback.correct: Professional mediation keeps circles healthy. CircleUp provides documentation tools and, if needed, platform mediation support.
feedback.incorrect: As organizer, you set the tone. Document issues professionally and use CircleUp's mediation support if disputes escalate.

organizer.question: What's the most important factor when setting your circle's contribution amount?

options.text: The highest amount possible to maximize payouts
An amount all members can realistically afford consistently
The same amount as other circles on the platform
Whatever the first member to join suggests

feedback.correct: Affordability is key! Circles fail when contributions are too high. CircleUp's calculator helps you find the sweet spot.
feedback.incorrect: Sustainable contributions = successful circles. Set amounts that all members can pay consistently, not just what's aspirational.

organizer.question: A member misses a payment and the Emergency Fund covers it. What happens next?

options.text: Nothing—that's what the fund is for
The member is removed immediately
The member repays the fund over time while the circle continues normally
You must cover the difference personally

feedback.correct: The Emergency Fund covers the immediate gap, and the defaulting member repays the fund gradually. Circle continuity is maintained.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp's Emergency Fund covers defaults automatically. The member then repays the fund—you don't have to manage recovery.

organizer.question: How should you handle the payout order for your circle?

options.text: Always give yourself the first payout as organizer
Let members choose or use random/Trust Score based methods for fairness
Assign order based on who you like most
Order doesn't matter—everyone gets the same amount

feedback.correct: Fair payout order builds trust. CircleUp offers fixed, random, bidding, and Trust Score methods—transparency is key.
feedback.incorrect: Fair, transparent payout order is essential. Use CircleUp's built-in methods rather than personal preference.

organizer.question: What's the main benefit of CircleUp's automated payment collection for you as an organizer?

options.text: You can take extra fees from members
You eliminate hours of chasing payments and awkward conversations
Members can't see when they're supposed to pay
You can delay payments to members you don't like

feedback.correct: Exactly! No more chasing, no more awkward money conversations. Payments happen automatically, preserving relationships.
feedback.incorrect: Automation saves you 10+ hours weekly on payment management and eliminates the relationship strain of chasing money.

organizer.question: A potential member asks why they should join your circle instead of a traditional one. What's your best answer?

options.text: Traditional circles are outdated and don't work
CircleUp adds transparency, protection, and automation while honoring the tradition
You'll make more money with CircleUp
There's no real difference

feedback.correct: CircleUp enhances tradition, not replaces it. Same community bonds, same savings power—plus modern protection and convenience.
feedback.incorrect: Position CircleUp as an enhancement to tradition: same community spirit, better transparency, protection, and automation.

organizer.question: Your circle is halfway through and you need to add a new member to replace someone who left. How does this work?

options.text: It's impossible—circles can't add members mid-cycle
The new member takes over the position, and CircleUp calculates their obligations
You have to restart the entire circle
The new member pays nothing and just receives a payout

feedback.correct: CircleUp handles mid-cycle additions smoothly, calculating exactly what the new member owes based on the payout position.
feedback.incorrect: CircleUp supports member replacement mid-cycle. The system calculates fair obligations for joining members.

organizer.question: What should you do before starting your first circle on CircleUp?

options.text: Jump in immediately—you'll learn as you go
Use the Circle Size Calculator and review the organizer guide
Wait until you have 50+ interested members
Create multiple circles at once to maximize earnings

feedback.correct: Planning pays off! The Circle Size Calculator helps optimize your configuration, and the organizer guide covers best practices.
feedback.incorrect: Use CircleUp's planning tools before launching. The Circle Size Calculator and organizer guide set you up for success.

organizer.question: How do you ensure your circle completes successfully?

options.text: Threaten members who might not pay
Vet members carefully, enable automated payments, and maintain clear communication
Keep the circle as large as possible for higher payouts
Don't worry—the platform guarantees success

feedback.correct: Success comes from good member selection, automation, and communication. CircleUp provides the tools; you provide the leadership.
feedback.incorrect: Successful circles start with careful vetting, use automation to prevent issues, and maintain transparent communication.
